Certainly! Here's a comprehensive prompt tailored for your book project, codenamed "Atlas." This prompt is designed to help you consistently organize, summarize, and extract content from your transcripts, ensuring a uniform structure and naming convention for all your data.

📘 Prompt for Organizing and Extracting Book Content

Objective: Systematically process and organize all transcript content related to the book project "Atlas," ensuring each entry includes a comprehensive summary, a structured table of contents, and a complete extraction of the transcript content.​

Instructions:

Metadata Inclusion:

Assign a unique identifier to each transcript entry using the format: Atlas_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.​

Record the exact date and time of the original chat or transcript.​
Catalog
+5
Prompt Advance
+5
Leadsync
+5

Summary Generation:

Provide a concise summary capturing the essence of the transcript.​

Ensure the tone aligns with the overarching theme of "Atlas," incorporating elements of darkness and the motif of "smoke" as per the book's style.​

Table of Contents Creation:

List all major topics or sections discussed in the transcript.​

Use clear and descriptive headings that reflect the content's depth and tone.​

Transcript Extraction:

Extract the entire content of the transcript verbatim.​

Ensure the text is clean, free from errors, and formatted for readability.​

Consistent Naming Convention:

Save each processed file using the naming format: Atlas_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_Summary.txt.​

Maintain a centralized index or log that records all entries with their corresponding metadata for easy retrieval.​

Output Format:

sql
Copy
Edit
Title: Atlas - [Unique Identifier]

Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
Time: [HH:MM:SS]

Summary:
[Concise summary in the tone of "Atlas," incorporating thematic elements.]

Table of Contents:
1. [First major topic]
2. [Second major topic]
...
n. [Nth major topic]

Transcript:
[Full, verbatim transcript content]
Additional Notes:

Ensure that all summaries and headings resonate with the book's dark and smoky aesthetic.​

Regularly back up the centralized index to prevent data loss.​

Review and update the naming conventions and formatting guidelines periodically to maintain consistency as the project evolves.​

By following this prompt, you'll establish a consistent and efficient system for managing your book's content, making future revisions and references more streamlined.
